change.summary: files.upload deprecated and sunset; apps created after the cutoff were blocked outright and received {"ok": false, "error": "method_deprecated"}. Callers had to move to a two-call sequence.

spec.note: A spec existed and was watchable, so this counts as a miss rather than an absent signal. It was last pushed 2021-09-07 and the repo was archived 2024-03-27 — two weeks BEFORE the deprecation was announced. The published document contains files.upload seven times and getUploadURLExternal zero times. A spec differ watching this repo would have seen nothing, ever.

changelog.note: Found only by reading the body: the URL slug is 'a-better-way-to-upload-files-is-here-to-stay' while the title is 'files.upload retires in March 2025'. Slug- or headline-based triage would misclassify this as a feature announcement.

headers.note: Slack signals deprecation in the JSON body ({"ok": false, "error": "method_deprecated"}), not via RFC 8594 Sunset or RFC 9745 Deprecation headers. A header probe finds nothing here.

contract.note: Calling the endpoint with an EXISTING app's credentials kept succeeding — only apps created after the cutoff were blocked. So contract verification from an established repo would have seen a healthy endpoint. The people who broke were those building new apps against old code, which is invisible to spec diffs, header probes and live calls alike.

notes: effective_at uses the new-app cutoff, which is when real breakage began (Superset hit it 2024-09-30), not the sunset. The sunset itself moved from 2025-03-11 to 2025-11-12 (announced 2025-03-17), and no primary source confirms it actually happened — the method reference page was still in future tense when checked on 2026-09-19. Marked partial for a second reason: the announcement post was EDITED IN PLACE. The archived April 2024 copy says the cutoff was 2024-05-08; the live copy at the same URL now says 2024-05-16. A monitor diffing that page would see a date silently change with no new entry in any feed.
